key_insight: Wire-based corner fillet friction stir welding can continuously feed filler metal to form load-bearing fillet welds with a controlled throat thickness.
engineering_relevance: This offers a solid-state alternative for producing stronger T- and corner-joint fillets in aluminum structures where conventional friction stir welding has limited access and insufficient material supply.
method: Continuously transport filler wire through a rotating extrusion screw into the internal corner region.
Use a stationary shoulder to confine and shape the plasticised material.
Produce single- and double-sided fillet geometries in 3.0 mm EN AW-6082-T6 sheets with EN AW-6082 filler wire.
evidence_signal: Cross-sections showed characteristic FSW zones without macroscopic pores or voids, and testing gave 231.55 MPa and 217.49 MPa tensile strengths with 66% and 62% joint efficiency.
watch_item: The process still needs careful control of supplied filler volume and access geometry, and the demonstrated results are based on limited specimen thickness and material system.
paper_title: Feasibility Study on the Production of Fillet Welds with Defined Throat Thickness Using Wire-Based Corner Fillet Friction Stir Welding
